profile.nameNote: Houhere and lacebark are shared by other Hoheria species.
profile.summary: A native tree of streamside forest in central New Zealand. Its tangled juvenile growth develops into a taller tree with larger leaves.
profile.lookFor: Toothed, pointed adult leaves and grey bark; white flowers are followed by winged dry fruit. Juvenile leaves are smaller and rounder.

profile.summary: An endemic shrub or small tree with spreading branches. Its leaves are divided into several broad, leathery leaflets.
profile.lookFor: Three to five leaflets radiating from a long stalk, with coarse teeth toward their ends. Small flowers occur in branched umbels and fruit darkens almost to black.

profile.summary: An endemic small shrub with a dense tangle of widely spreading twigs. Its small leaves vary considerably in shape.
profile.lookFor: Tiny paired leaves clustered on fine branches, often unequal in a pair. Small dark-red berries are a useful seasonal feature.

profile.lookFor: Leathery opposite leaves taper to sharp tips. Summer flowers have masses of red projecting stamens; mature bark flakes in thin strips.

profile.summary: An aromatic native shrub of eastern South Island scrub. Fine branchlets and tiny scale leaves give it a cypress-like outline.
profile.lookFor: Slender green to blue-green branchlets with small triangular leaves clasping the stem. Small pale blue or mauve flowers occur near the tips.
